questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make tea without sugar
Why oil is causing a climate emergency
The eating habits of English kings and queens in the past
How our addiction to sugar developed through history
questions.why: Georgie asks how our addiction to the sweet stuff began – that's what they discuss.

questions.q: What does Georgie do when she makes Neil's tea?
options: She puts in only one sugar instead of three
She puts in three sugars, exactly as he asked her
She forgets the milk
She makes it with no sugar at all
questions.why: She says, “here's your tea, Neil… I just put one sugar.”

questions.q: What does Neil compare our addiction to sugar with?
options: Our addiction to coffee
Our addiction to oil
Our addiction to phones
Our addiction to tobacco
questions.why: He says just as our addiction to oil causes a climate emergency, sugar causes a health emergency.

questions.q: What was sugar like when it first came to England?
options: Cheap, and eaten by almost everyone in the country
Only used as medicine
An expensive luxury only the rich could afford
Banned by the king
questions.why: Neil says it was an expensive luxury affordable only to kings, queens and the very rich.

questions.q: How was sugar produced for four hundred years?
options: In small farms across England
In big factories in the United States and across Europe
By trading companies in Asia only
On plantations using slaves, then shipped to Europe
questions.why: Georgie says it was grown in slavery plantations and shipped across the Atlantic to Europe.

questions.q: What comparison does Professor Ulbe Bosma make?
options: Sugar was more valuable than gold
It fuelled bodies, as oil later fuelled vehicles
Sugar and coffee were equally popular
Sugar was used to power the very first steam engines
questions.why: He says sugar became the fuel for human bodies, whereas oil became the fuel for vehicles.

questions.q: What did sugar companies do when people learned about sugar's health problems?
options: They added sugar to foods like bread and yogurt
They stopped selling sugar
They made sugar more expensive
They paid for health campaigns about eating less sugar
questions.why: Georgie says they began using sugar in food which had previously contained none.

questions.q: Why does Professor Bosma compare a few spoons a week with a kilo today?
options: To show that sugar is cheaper today
To show how much people's eating habits have changed
To explain how sugar is measured
To suggest that eating a kilo a week is perfectly healthy
questions.why: He says eating habits had to change: from a few spoons a week to a kilo today.
